audits.title: 1382 Retrospective Audit to Assess Compliance to National Guidance for The Follow-Up of Acute Uncomplicated Diverticulitis and Adenoma Detection Rate at University Hospital Bristol
audits.standard: UK guidance: follow-up outpatient LGI endoscopy 6-8 weeks after discharge for uncomplicated diverticulitis

cycle1.result: 42% (179/426) had LGI endoscopy; 23% (99/426) within the 8-week target; median time to outpatient endoscopy 70 days (6-287).

audits.other_findings: Polyps in 21% (37/179), tubular adenoma 5% (9/179), one high grade dysplasia, no malignancy; authors question necessity of routine endoscopy.
audits.citation: Newton L, Huppler L, McCabe T, Gourbault L, Embury-Young Y, Handa I, et al.. 1382 Retrospective Audit to Assess Compliance to National Guidance for The Follow-Up of Acute Uncomplicated Diverticulitis and Adenoma Detection Rate at University Hospital Bristol. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.428.

audits.title: TU2.3 Flexible sigmoidoscopy after management of CT proven uncomplicated acute diverticulitis: a closed loop audit of local practice at tertiary care centre
audits.standard: WSES recommendations: flexible sigmoidoscopy not required after CT-proven uncomplicated acute diverticulitis without red flags
audits.setting: Tertiary care centre, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust; inpatients and ambulatory care unit

cycle1.result: 80 of 115 admissions (69.5%) had CT-proven UAD; 39 (48.8%) booked for flexible sigmoidoscopy; 10 (25.64%) had sub-centimetre polyps.

cycle2.result: 34 of 49 patients had UAD; 10 (29.4%) underwent flexible sigmoidoscopy; polyps in 3 (8.8%).

audits.other_findings: Low rate of positive findings suggests outpatient sigmoidoscopy requests in uncomplicated cases were unjustified.
audits.citation: Ahsan A, Ma J, Krasicka D, Ray K, Swaminathan C, Sajid M. TU2.3 Flexible sigmoidoscopy after management of CT proven uncomplicated acute diverticulitis: a closed loop audit of local practice at tertiary care centre. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.015.

audits.title: FP3.5 - Colonoscopy post diverticulitis – Compliance with ACPGBI guidance in a single centre audit
audits.standard: ACPGBI guidance on colonoscopy after diverticulitis

cycle1.result: 90 uncomplicated diverticulitis without surgery: 71 (59% of total) had colonoscopy, 19 (16%) did not; 78.9% of uncomplicated cases had colonoscopy, which may have been unnecessary. Complicated: 15 surgery, 15 no surgery, 11 (9.2%) colonoscopy, 4 (3.3%) no colonoscopy.

audits.other_findings: Of 82 patients who had colonoscopy, no colorectal cancer was detected (0%); 3.3% of complicated cases had no colonoscopy due to patient choice, comorbidities or frailty. FIT suggested as an adjunct.
audits.citation: Castelhano R, Helmy N, Linzell A, Davies E. FP3.5 - Colonoscopy post diverticulitis – Compliance with ACPGBI guidance in a single centre audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.362.

audits.title: 711 A Retrospective Audit on the Management and Follow Up Practices of Acute Diverticulitis
audits.standard: ACPGBI emergency colorectal surgery guidelines on acute diverticulitis and follow-up endoscopy

cycle1.result: 41/106 (39%) with an indication had no follow-up endoscopy; 42/55 without an indication had endoscopy; antibiotics given to all but 2 uncomplicated patients and 85% admitted.

audits.other_findings: Unindicated endoscopies cost an excess £35,202; four malignancy/high-grade dysplasia lesions found only in the indicated group.
audits.citation: Perera H, Ashoush F, Inglis E, Samaradiwakara S, Noblett S. 711 A Retrospective Audit on the Management and Follow Up Practices of Acute Diverticulitis. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.239.

audits.title: EP 591 Follow-Up Colonoscopy in Acute Diverticulitis: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Adherence
audits.standard: WSES and ESCP guidelines: colonoscopy 6-8 weeks after complicated diverticulitis

cycle1.result: 1 of 21 colonoscopies within 6-8 weeks; timely colonoscopy in 5% of complicated cases; 1 malignancy.

cycle2.result: 6 of 18 complicated cases had timely colonoscopy; overall 46% of complicated cases timely; no malignancies.

audits.other_findings: Same abstract as DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.393; routine colonoscopy for uncomplicated cases should be reconsidered.
audits.citation: Elsalahi M, Sajol M, Jabeen S, Elsllabi M, Toor A. EP 591 Follow-Up Colonoscopy in Acute Diverticulitis: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Adherence. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.629.

audits.title: EP 687 Are we Overscoping?: An Audit of Colonoscopic Follow-up in Acute Diverticulitis Management
audits.standard: ASGBI and ACPGBI: endoscopic evaluation at 6-8 weeks only for complicated diverticulitis (Hinchey 2 and above)

cycle1.result: Hinchey score recorded in 8.7% (10/115); 27 uncomplicated cases had unnecessary follow-up colonoscopy.

audits.other_findings: No sinister findings or malignancy in the over-investigated group.
audits.citation: Lagunathan S, Aspari A, Mehaina T, Soundararajan K. EP 687 Are we Overscoping?: An Audit of Colonoscopic Follow-up in Acute Diverticulitis Management. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.644.
